mission: Owner decision 2026-10-19 14:48Z: add the ops-write runbook apply-migration, the only path for a schema migration to reach staging (owner click per run in staging-ops; agents never approve). It allowlists exactly revision 7a52e9b48e8a on parent 3b7d9c1a5e20 and refuses anything else; before any write it requires a Railway Postgres backup younger than 24 h (scripts/staging_backup_age.py), a passing read-only fingerprint and live alembic_version equal to the parent. A dry run (default) writes nothing and reports the SQL plan and its SHA-256, the lock budget and row counts; apply needs that SHA and runs only that revision in one transaction with lock_timeout 5 s and statement_timeout 120 s, then records the new revision. This PR applies no migration and changes no schema, collector, source, price, identity, mapping, Market Value/Index, secret or Railway setting. Staging only; PSA10 untouched.

impacts.reason: New write runbook apply-migration registered in RUNBOOKS as write and collector-affecting (quiet windows 02:00-06:00 and 19:30-20:30 UTC apply to an apply). Preflight refuses any revision/parent pair outside ALLOWED. The runbook refuses unless this checkout has the migration as its only head, the backup is under 24 h, the fingerprint passes and live alembic_version is the parent; the dry run opens only the default_transaction_read_only session. Nothing runs in this PR.

Adds apply-migration to the runbook choice and two string inputs, revision and parent, passed through env to both jobs. No permission, secret, environment, trigger or approval change; the owner-approval job still holds no credential.

Refuse paths (wrong revision, wrong parent, missing from checkout, extra head, no backup, stale backup, already applied, live not parent, SHA mismatch), lock parsing, the writable-engine option, workflow wiring, and on Postgres in a throwaway schema: dry run writes nothing, apply then already applied, failure rolls back everything, lock_timeout bounds the wait.
Documents apply-migration and its dispatch inputs; the delivery doc now points migrations at the runbook instead of a manual railway run.

recovery.procedure: Native revert of this PR removes the runbook and its workflow choice. No data, schema, provider or service configuration to undo.
recovery.trigger: An apply-migration run that writes on a dry run, accepts a pair outside ALLOWED, or runs without a fresh backup.
recovery.backup: Not applicable to this PR: no schema or row change. A later apply requires a Railway Postgres backup under 24 h before it writes.
